text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Thirty countries will announce their contributions towards the reconstruction drive in Lebanon in the "Friends of Lebanon" conference being held in Washington today for this purpose.
-Lebanon bans the import of cattles from Bulgary.

-Israeli Brigadier-General Eli Amitay, commander of Israel's liason unit to south Lebanon was lightly injured and three geurrilla fighters were killed in a guerrilla attack against Israeli patrol in the south on Saturday.
-Lebanon expects more than $1 billion in loans from the "Friends of Lebanon" conference.
-Three American companies will finance a tourist project in Lebanon worth $200 million.
-Prime Minister Hariri rules out any wide Israeli operation against Lebanon
-Sibline cement company gets a $57.5 million loan from five Lebanese banks.
-Christian Maronite Patriarch says the rich Lebanese can reconstruct their country if they feel their money would be secure.
-A five-nation ceasefire monitoring committee will meet today to discuss the Israeli complaint that a Katyusha rocket attack on its northern area violated a ceasefire in south Lebanon.
-Lebanon is accessible to those who want a political role, Parliament Speaker says.
